topic: Decoding Epidemics: The SIR Model Mechanics

outline.topic: Decoding Epidemics: The SIR Model Mechanics

sections.title: The Hook: Why do diseases spread?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of population dynamics using a simple analogy. Establish the three states of an individual: Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R).
sections.example: Imagine a 'Z-day' scenario in a high school cafeteria: students who are healthy (S), those who catch a 'zombie-flu' (I), and those who become immune/healed (R).

sections.title: Visualizing the Flow: The SIR Engine
sections.content: Explain the transition rates between states. Introduce the differential equations through visual 'pipes' (S → I → R) where the speed of flow is determined by contact rate (β) and recovery rate (γ).
sections.example: Visualize the population as three connected transparent tanks. The rate at which the 'S' tank drains into the 'I' tank depends on how many 'Zombies' are currently roaming.

sections.title: The Mathematical Pulse: Reproduction Number (R0)
sections.content: Define R0 (R-naught) as the average number of secondary infections caused by one infected individual. Use a graphical tree diagram to show how R0 > 1 leads to exponential growth.
sections.example: Show a character 'Patient Zero' infecting 3 friends (R0=3), then those 3 infecting 9 more, creating a rapidly branching visual tree.

sections.title: Simulation & Intervention: Flattening the Curve
sections.content: Demonstrate how changing parameters (like social distancing) shrinks the 'β' value. Show the movement of the epidemic peak visually using a time-series line graph.
sections.example: Animation of a 'Social Distancing' barrier appearing in the simulation, showing how the 'Infected' curve flattens and stretches over a longer time period.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: SIR models are tools for prediction, not crystal balls. Emphasize that parameters (β and γ) are the levers policymakers use to control outbreaks.
sections.example: A final infographic overlaying a real-world scenario (e.g., vaccine rollout) onto the SIR model curves to show the reduction of the 'Susceptible' pool.

storyboard.title: The Hook: Why do diseases spread?
lecture_lines: Individuals move between three distinct states.
Infected individuals eventually recover or gain immunity.
animations: Create a central 'Population Cloud' of white dots (label: #FFFFFF).
Highlight a 'Patient Zero' dot in bright red (#FF0000).
Show transmission from red dot to adjacent white dots (color: #FF5555).

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Flow: The SIR Engine
lecture_lines: States behave like connected fluid tanks.
Contact rates drive Susceptible to Infected.
Recovery rates move Infected to Recovered.
animations: Display three boxes: S (blue, #0000FF), I (red, #FF0000), R (green, #00FF00).
Animate dots moving from S-box to I-box (flow visual).
Animate dots moving from I-box to R-box (flow visual).

storyboard.title: The Mathematical Pulse: Reproduction Number (R0)
animations: Display equation 'R0 = beta * c * d' in center (color: #FFFF00).
Flash 'beta' while showing a transmission connection.
Flash 'c' while showing a network contact diagram.

storyboard.title: Simulation & Intervention: Flattening the Curve
animations: Show a rising infection curve graph (color: #FF0000).
Animate a horizontal line 'Intervention' lowering the curve.

storyboard.title: Summary & Synthesis
animations: Flash 'R0' above the model, then fade in 'Intervention'.
